document_metadata.document_title: Stormwater Management Manual for Western Washington (Ecology 2024; city MS4)

design_criteria.water_quality_volume_method: Adopts Ecology SWMMWW Minimum Requirements including runoff treatment and flow control; continuous simulation (WWHM/HSPF) sizes flow control. Local stormwater code supplements SWMMWW.

evidence.excerpt: City of Bellingham MS4 follows Ecology SWMMWW
Document that the maximum ponded depth from the infiltration BMP can infiltrate through the infiltration BMP surface within 48 hours.
UIC wells are designed to completely drain ponded runoff within 48 to 72 hours after flow to the UIC well has stopped.
The minimum vertical separation is 5 feet between the base of a UIC well and the highest elevation between the seasonal high groundwater table, bedrock, hardpan, or other low-permeability layer.
The base of BMP T7.10: Infiltration Ponds or BMP T7.20: Infiltration Trenches shall be ≥ 5 feet above the seasonal high-water mark, bedrock (or hardpan) or other low permeability layer.
The "Default" and "Custom" BSM depth must be 18 inches to provide Runoff Treatment and good growing conditions for selected plants.

extraction_quality.review_notes: Municipality coverage via Ecology SWMMWW (Everett/Olympia pattern). City may publish a local drainage manual separately.

design_parameters.enrich_notes: Ecology SWMMWW excerpts: infiltration drawdown check is 48 h ponded depth; UIC wells cite 48–72 h drain. SHWT separation varies by BMP (5 ft / 60 in general for infiltration ponds, trenches, and UIC presumptive; 3 ft / 36 in may be allowed with analysis; 1 ft / 12 in below permeable pavement lowest layer and small bioretention; 3 ft below bioretention for larger contributing areas). BSM default/custom media depth 18 in. Site infeasibility below 0.3 in/hr native Ksat; long-term design infiltration up to 3 in/hr; BSM end-of-life Ksat 12 in/hr for sizing. Wet pond permanent pool max depth concern above 8 ft (96 in). Permeable pavement treatment sand layers 6 in or 12 in; minimum surface slope 1–2%. Biofiltration swales on sites slope less than 6%.
